articles.title: Commanders’ Tyler Owens goes viral after bulldozing Eagles blockers on insane special teams play
articles.summary: Tyler Owens just produced one of the wildest special teams plays you’ll see all season.
articles.body:
Tyler Owens just produced one of the wildest special teams plays you’ll see all season.

The Commanders safety came flying down the field on punt coverage against the Eagles, and apparently decided blockers weren’t going to stop him.

Owens powered straight through multiple Philadelphia players before getting to returner Britain Covey and slamming him to the ground.

The play immediately took off online, with fans stunned by the sheer physicality of it.

And Owens didn’t just make the tackle.

He basically went through everyone Philadelphia put in his way to get there.

The Eagles ultimately won the season opener 24-22, but Owens definitely delivered one of the plays of the game.

articles.title: The tackle everyone is talking about: Commanders’ Tyler Owens delivers NFL’s best special teams play
articles.standfirst: The Washington player powered through both blockers, maintained his balance, and finished the tackle on a return specialist
articles.summary: The Washington player powered through both blockers, maintained his balance, and finished the tackle on a return specialist
articles.body:
Special teams rarely command national attention. Touchdown passes, game-changing interceptions, and explosive runs usually dominate the conversation on NFL Sundays. But Washington Commanders safety Tyler Owens managed to steal the spotlight in Week 1 with a play that had some of the biggest names in football raving.

In Washington's 24-22 season-opening loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Owens recorded just two tackles in the official box score. On paper, it looked like a relatively quiet afternoon for a player whose primary role comes on special teams.

The film told a completely different story

During a punt return, Owens produced what many are already calling one of the best special teams plays of the young NFL season. Racing downfield in coverage, the third-year safety encountered a double team designed to take him out of the play. Instead, he powered through both blockers, maintained his balance, and finished the tackle on return specialist Britain Covey.

The effort was so extraordinary that future Pro Football Hall of Famer J.J. Watt immediately took notice. "One of the greatest football plays I've ever seen," Watt said. He went even further, adding that "every coach in America will be showing this rep to their team this week."

That is not the kind of praise typically reserved for a special teams tackle. Even Tom Brady, now serving as a broadcaster, highlighted the play during the game and praised Owens' relentless effort. What made the sequence remarkable was not simply the tackle itself, but the determination required to complete it. Most coverage players would have been erased from the play after encountering two blockers in space.

Owens used speed and pursuit angles to work around traffic

Owens refused to accept that outcome, fighting through contact and turning what should have been a positive return for Philadelphia into a momentum-changing stop. As impressive as that play was, it wasn't even Tyler's only standout moment of the afternoon.

His second tackle on special teams showcased a different skill set. Instead of muscling through blockers, Owens used speed and pursuit angles to work around traffic. When Covey attempted to make him miss in the open field, Tyler stayed under control and delivered another textbook tackle.

Taken together, the two plays offered a masterclass in special teams coverage. It's the type of performance that often goes unnoticed outside meeting rooms, where coaches obsess over fundamentals, effort, and execution. Yet Owens' contributions became impossible to ignore.

The performance also served as a reminder of the journey Tyler has taken to reach this point. After going undrafted in 2024, Owens faced long odds to carve out a place in the NFL. He earned a roster spot with Washington and has gradually established himself as one of the team's most dependable special teams contributors.

articles.title: Dorance Armstrong Reappears Like a Ghost on the Dallas Cowboys' Path
articles.standfirst: The Washington Commanders’ defensive end has returned from suspension in time to play the Cowboys
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders’ defensive end has returned from suspension in time to play the Cowboys
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have received a boost ahead of their upcoming Dallas Cowboys matchup, with defensive end Dorance Armstrong reinstated after serving a one-game suspension following the season opener.

Armstrong 's return comes just in time for the Commanders ' meeting with his former team, with the defensive end now available after missing the opening game of the 2026 campaign while serving his league-imposed ban.

KPRC 2 Houston reporter and NFL insider Aaron Wilson announced Armstrong's reinstatement from suspension on September 16 through X.com, formerly known as Twitter.

“#NFL lifts #Commanders Dorance Armstrong suspension,” Wilson wrote, offering relief to the defensive end, who had been suspended from August 30 after violating the league's personal conduct policy.

Armstrong's suspension followed his May 2025 arrest in Frisco, Texas. ESPN reported that he faced misdemeanor charges involving bodily harm and resisting arrest or a search of his vehicle following the incident.

The former Cowboys defender received deferred adjudication for both charges and nine months of probation. The NFL then issued a one-game suspension, which cost Armstrong $507,500 in salary and bonus money.

The ban also delayed his return from a torn ACL suffered during Week 7 of the 2025 season. He had already spent significant time recovering before the suspension ruled him out of the team's opener.

Drafted by Dallas in the fourth round of the 2018 NFL Draft, Armstrong spent six seasons with the Cowboys before signing a three-year, $33 million contract with the Commanders ahead of 2024.

The defensive end initially remained on the physically unable to perform list, but received clearance on August 7, and he subsequently returned to individual drills as he continued building towards a full comeback.

The Commanders will hope Armstrong can provide an immediate boost against the Cowboys after opening the season with a narrow defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles , and his experience could be particularly useful against his former team.

Across 116 NFL appearances, Armstrong has registered 137 solo tackles, 34 sacks and five forced fumbles. His development was aided by Dan Quinn , who later became the Commanders ' head coach.

Armstrong can rush from the edge with his hand in the dirt or move inside during sub-packages, potentially allowing Washington to deploy other pass rushers such as Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson around him.

Stefon Diggs penalised for touchdown celebration

Meanwhile, the Commanders ’ opener also featured an unwanted moment involving Stefon Diggs , whose touchdown celebration brought a 15-yard penalty as the receiver climbed onto the goalpost padding after scoring against the Eagles .

After a quiet opening period, Diggs found more involvement during the fourth quarter before creating separation and scoring in the red zone his touchdown briefly gave Washington hope of victory.

But as Diggs jumped onto the goalpost padding and embraced it, the team collected a 15-yard penalty in accordance with the NFL ’s rules and the infraction moved the Commanders out of two-point conversion range.

Diggs had already experienced the same punishment back in 2017 playing against Washington , as he hugged the goalpost after scoring and was subsequently fined $12,154 by the NFL.

"That was a little bit out of frustration throughout the game," Diggs admitted. "[I] wanted things to go right and finally, we hit one. I get a little overzealous, I get a little excited. Of course, I take full accountability."

Although Diggs later accepted responsibility for the mistake, for the Commanders , the incident became another frustrating detail from a narrow opening-day defeat.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels suffers shocking injury as Tom Brady reacts: “Oh, s*!”**
articles.standfirst: Jayden Daniels’ scary elbow injury leaves Commanders fearing the worst
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels’ scary elbow injury leaves Commanders fearing the worst
articles.body:
T om Brady reacted like any fan when he saw the alarming injury suffered by Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels near the end of the first half against the Dallas Cowboys .

The former quarterback, now a Fox Sports analys t, was visibly stunned watching the replay of the play in which Daniels’ left elbow bent in a concerning way after a fall at AT&T Stadium.

“Oh, s***,” Brady exclaimed on the broadcast.

The seven-time Super Bowl champion quickly apologized for his reaction and explained that he hadn’t expected to see such a graphic image.

“Sorry. I wasn’t expecting to see that,” he said.

The injury occurred on the final play before halftime. Daniels was stepped on while receiving the ball near the Dallas goal line, lost his balance, and fell to the turf. As he tried to brace himself, he put his left arm down and suffered an injury that immediately recalled the elbow dislocation that sidelined him last season.

Although a definitive diagnosis has not yet been announced, the Commanders confirmed that Daniels would not return to the game due to the left elbow injur y. He was carted to the locker room while Marcus Mariota took over the offense for the second half.

Concern is heightened because Daniels suffered a similar injury a year ago—an elbow dislocation that forced him to miss four games. After returning, he reaggravated the same area and did not play again that season.

Following a historic rookie campaign in which he emerged as one of the NFL’s brightest young stars, Daniels appeared in only seven games last season due to physical issues. Washington is now hoping this latest injury does not carry more serious consequences.

Daniels was not the only player to leave the game with an injury late in the second quarter. Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant also exited after suffering a hamstring injury when he was accidentally stepped on by teammate Markquese Bell. Durant was sent to the locker room and later ruled out for the remainder of the contest.
